name: remote-mobile-native
goal: A phone keeps a scoped, purgeable read cache, exposes only attached methods, accepts a public pairing link, and its native session rules are proven by real Swift checks

evidence: Scope from the continuation brief: (1) native cache in the app cache directory, file-protected, not backed up, keyed by origin/host/device/generation/grant and method+input; media hash-checked; cached answers carry a saved time and are read-only; purge on denial, revocation, changed host/device/grant; late answers never stored; no drafts in it. (2) Swift driver under ios/Checks for stale channel callbacks, revocation, vault/cache authority, uncertain mutations, 307/308/WebSocket redirects, Release refusing loopback. (3) bridge exposes only attached methods. (4) harnessremote://pair deep link with public ids only, code typed in app; safe areas with viewport-fit=cover. (5) placeholder component tests removed. Proof: red-green JS unit and E2E with frozen files, native checks Debug and Release, simulator build and inspected screenshot. No live relay or host proof is claimed.

Native: RemoteCache (scoped by origin, host, device, generation, grant; file-protected; no backup; media hash-checked; purge on revocation, changed authority and refusals), attached methods kept in the record and enforced, pairing deep link with scheme harnessremote, Debug-only loopback and open-link switches, session split into core, pairing, reads, authority, link, events. Renderer: remoteGrant, cachedSnapshot, remoteAuthority, bridge offers only attached methods and marks saved snapshots, phone store reads saved copies once when opened offline and keeps an offered link, lock state shown only when reported, safe areas. Unsigned simulator build launches; link reaches the page through the real plugin with the Debug launch argument. No real relay or host was used.
